title: Dynamic Fidelity Gating PRD & Rollout Playbook
author: Aisha Martinez
body:
Summary:

This PRD defines Dynamic Fidelity Gating (DFG): a product capability that lets customers automatically modulate output fidelity (model variant, decoding temperature, token budget, quantization profile) per-request based on business policies, cost budget, latency SLOs, and explicit per-route quality constraints. DFG provides an API surface, control plane, and observability contract enabling safe, measurable reductions in serving cost while bounding user-facing quality regressions.

Background and motivation:

- Customers want predictable unit economics for inference without permanently sacrificing quality.
- Static fidelity tiers are blunt instruments: they force coarse tradeoffs and require manual migrations.
- Operators need automated, auditable mechanisms to reduce cost during capacity pressure or to meet dynamic budget constraints while preserving critical responses at higher fidelity.

Goals (what success looks like):

1. Provide an SDK + HTTP control API to define per-tenant/per-route gating policies (time windows, cost budget, latency thresholds, fidelity budget).
2. Implement an in-path router that evaluates requests against policies and selects a fidelity variant deterministically and efficiently (<= 1ms decision overhead).
3. Ship telemetry that attributes cost, latency, and quality delta to gating decisions with drift detection and regression alerts.
4. Support safe rollouts with canary, percentage-based traffic shifting, and automatic rollback triggers based on quality guardrails.

Non-goals:

- This PRD does not cover low-level kernel optimizations or new quantization kernels (runtime team will implement runtime hooks separately).
- Not a replacement for long-term model retraining to improve cost/quality tradeoffs.

High-level design overview:

- Control plane: policy registry, evaluation engine, rollout manager, audit log.
- Data plane: fast fidelity selector injected in request path that yields a fidelity descriptor (variant id, decode params, quantization tag).

Key concepts and terminology:

- Fidelity descriptor: the bundle of choices for a request (model variant, qprofile, token cap, sampling params).
- Gating policy: rules that map request/context signals -> fidelity descriptor candidates with priority and constraints.
- Guardrail: observable thresholds (e.g., latency P95, generation acceptance rate, eval-based quality score) that, when violated, trigger rollback or traffic reroute.

Product requirements (numbered):

1) Policy definition API (MVP):
   - Support JSON-based policy objects with fields: target_scope, priority, match_conditions, candidates (ordered), constraints, rollout_config.
   - Example policy JSON (MVP):

```
{
  "policy_id": "policy-123",
  "target_scope": {"tenant_id": "acct-42", "route": "/chat/completions"},
  "priority": 10,
  "match_conditions": [{"header.user-agent": "mobile-app"}],
  "candidates": [
    {"variant": "rwl-1.0-high", "weight": 80},
    {"variant": "rwl-1.0-mid-quant", "weight": 20}
  ],
  "constraints": {"p95_latency_ms": 350, "max_cost_per_k": 8.0},
  "rollout_config": {"strategy": "gradual", "steps": [10, 25, 50, 100], "pause_on_violation": true}
}
```

2) Fidelity selector (data plane):
   - Latency budget for decision: <=1ms median, <=5ms p99 before request enters model scheduling queue.
   - Deterministic selection given request id + seed to ensure reproducible sampling for debugging.

3) Observability contract (must ship with MVP):
   - Emit per-request fields: fidelity_variant, selector_reason, estimated_unit_cost, decision_latency_ms, policy_id, policy_version, quality_score_hint.
   - Export aggregated metrics: fidelity_distribution_by_route, cost_saved_estimate, quality_regression_rate, policy_violation_count.

4) Quality measurement and regression detection:
   - Integrate with Eval capture pipeline: maintain small continuously-run prompt set per-tenant (configurable) that is scored monthly and on-rollout.
   - Define acceptable quality delta: default max 3% drop on tenant eval benchmark vs baseline; configurable per policy.

5) Rollout and safety mechanisms:
   - Canary rollout: support routing 0-100% with automated step progression or manual approvals.
   - Automatic pause/rollback triggers: sustained p95 latency increase > 15% for 10m OR quality delta > configured threshold OR error rate increase > 2x baseline.
   - Emergency override: admins can pin routes to highest-fidelity variant at any time.

6) Billing and unit economics integration:
   - Report cost attribution per-fidelity-variant in billing-ready format (daily aggregation per tenant/route/variant).
   - Allow policies to include max-cost ceilings; the control plane should reject policy updates that would exceed contracted commitments.

7) SDKs and CLI:
   - Provide Python + Typescript SDK to create/update/delete policies and query active selector decisions.
   - CLI: redwood dfg apply-policy --file policy.json; redwood dfg rollout status --policy policy-123

API contract (preview):

- Create policy (HTTP): POST /v1/dfg/policies  (Auth: token)
- Evaluate decision (HTTP, internal): POST /internal/dfg/evaluate -> returns {"variant": "rwl-1.0-mid-quant", "selector_ms": 0.7, "explanation": "cost_budget_trigger"}
- Query telemetry (HTTP): GET /v1/dfg/metrics?tenant=acct-42&from=2026-01-01&to=2026-01-07

Behavioral examples / decision matrix (table as text):

| Signal                 | Condition                          | Action (example)                            |
|------------------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Peak region load       | infrastructure_utilization > 85%   | Prefer quantized mid variants, cap tokens   |
| Tenant soft budget hit | projected_monthly_cost >= 90% cap  | Shift 20% of non-critical routes to mid-quant|
| Low-priority route     | route.label == "async_batch"      | Always use low-cost variant                 |
| High-risk prompt       | contains PII flagged by classifier  | Pin to high-fidelity variant                |

Observability and telemetry details:

- Required metrics (prometheus + traces):
  - dfg.selector.latency_ms (histogram)
  - dfg.variant.requests_total{variant,route,tenant}
  - dfg.cost.saved_estimate_total{tenant}
  - dfg.quality.delta{policy_id}
  - dfg.policy.violations_total{policy_id,reason}
- Traces: tag requests with fidelity.variant and policy.id. Span should include selector decision step.

- Dashboards (must ship with MVP):
  1. Per-tenant fidelity mix & cost impact (time series + heatmap)
  2. Policy health (violations, rollout status, recent rollbacks)
  3. Quality regression alerts table linked to eval snapshots

Testing and validation plan:

1) Unit and integration tests for policy language semantics (fuzz policies).
2) Synthetic traffic experiments: run A/B with seeded prompt library to measure objective quality delta and cost savings.
3) Staging rollout: enable on internal tenants only for 2 weeks, run daily eval.
4) Beta cohort: 5 customers covering low/medium/high throughput, one regulated vertical; gather feedback for 8 weeks.

Rollout playbook (step-by-step):

1. Feature flag behind org-level toggle; initial default: disabled for all customers.
2. Internal enablement: enable for Redwood internal tenant; monitor 72h.
3. Canary cohort: enable for non-production demo tenants (10% traffic) for 2 weeks.
4. Beta customers: enable per-contract with 1-week canary steps [10%, 25%, 50%, 100] with pause for manual review at each step.
4a. At each step run monthly eval suite on gated prompts and compare to baseline; if regression > policy threshold, automatically pause and notify reviewers.
5. General availability: after 8 weeks of stable beta + signoff from product, runtime, reliability, and security.

Failure modes and mitigation table (text):

- Incorrect policy match: include policy dry-run mode that logs decisions without enforcing; require 48h dry-run for any new targeting rule in production.
- Selector bias: ensure deterministic seed is derived from request.id and hashed with policy.version to avoid correlated sampling.
- Quality drift: maintain rolling monthly eval; if trend indicates drift > 1% per week, trigger rollback and model onboarding review.

Operational ownership and SLAs:

- Product: Aisha Martinez (PM, owner of policy UX and rollout criteria).
- Runtime: SRE lead for selector performance and kernel integration (owner: Marco Chen).
- Applied ML: responsible for eval suites and quality scoring (owner: Dr. Elena Rossi).
- On-call: selector service on-call rotation maintained by eng-serving-runtime team; target selector decision p99 < 5ms.

Compliance and security considerations:

- Policies must respect tenant data residency settings; DFG control plane will validate and reject cross-region candidate variants.
- Sensitive content classifier can opt-out matching to prevent gating from reducing fidelity on PII-sensitive prompts.

Open questions and implementation risks:

- How to estimate "quality_score_hint" cheaply at decision time? Proposal: use lightweight proxy classifier trained to estimate degradation risk per-variant.
- Cost model accuracy for atypical prompt shapes (very long context). Mitigation: require per-route calibration and periodically re-benchmark.

Timeline and milestones (high level):

- Q4 2025: Policy schema and API design, SDK prototypes, initial selector PoC.
- Q1 2026: Data plane selector implementation, telemetry contract, staging integration.
- Q2 2026: Beta customers and canary tooling, billing attribution export.
- Q3 2026: GA with full dashboarding and rollout automations.

Appendices:

A. Example CLI usage:
$ redwood dfg apply-policy --file policy.json --org acct-42
$ redwood dfg rollout status --policy policy-123 --watch

B. Example decision response (internal evaluate endpoint):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "variant": "rwl-1.0-mid-quant",
  "selector_ms": 0.8,
  "policy_id": "policy-123",
  "policy_version": "v2",
  "explanation": "cost_budget_trigger",
  "estimated_unit_cost": "0.0064",
  "quality_score_hint": "0.88"
}
```

C. Cross-team dependencies:
- Runtime: decision hook placement, kernel tags for variants.
- Billing: variant cost table and daily exports.
- Observability: new metrics and dashboard ownership.
- Security: review for tenancy/residency and emergency override controls.

D. Owner contact and escalation path:
- PM: Aisha Martinez (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Runtime lead: Marco Chen (marco@redwood.ai)
- On-call: eng-serving-runtime rotation via PagerDuty (DFG-selector service)

End of document.
